statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete. Search, product, cart, and sign-in failures were observed as direct core-flow issues rather than omitted checks.

page.framework: Amazon AUI / server-rendered MPA with client modules and service worker
page.notes: Public Canadian commerce storefront. Homepage was accessible; representative search, product, cart and sign-in routes failed or challenged fresh browser sessions. Covered homepage, search, one product detail, cart, sign-in, and a synthetic not-found state. Not covered: authenticated account, payment submission, order placement, cancellation/returns completion, and additional category/detail templates because sign-in and purchase routes were unavailable and no destructive or real transaction was attempted.

paths.description: Homepage and global retail navigation, representing the landing template and initial product-discovery entry point.
Search for “laptop”, representing the primary product-discovery journey. The route consistently returned Amazon’s generic error page during independent captures.
Representative product detail URL discovered from the homepage. Fresh sessions were diverted to an automated-access “Continue shopping” challenge instead of product content.
Cart route, representing the purchase funnel. It returned Amazon’s generic “Something went wrong” page.
Sign-in route, representing authentication and account entry. It returned a “Looking for Something?” not-found page.
Synthetic nonexistent route, representing HTTP/runtime failure recovery. It exposed a bilingual recovery screen with homepage/search routes.

findings.summary: Homepage is not mobile-responsive in the captured condition
findings.evidence: At 360x800, layout reported no viewport meta, a 1000px inner layout, and 640px overflow; the screenshot shows clipped desktop content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid width=device-width viewport and use intrinsic/grid layouts that reflow without horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Primary discovery and purchase routes fail in fresh sessions
findings.evidence: Search returned “Something went wrong”, product detail returned an automated-access challenge, cart returned the same generic error, and sign-in returned not-found.
findings.suggestedFix: Stabilise anonymous session/WAF routing so search, product, cart, and sign-in work end-to-end; retain context and provide route-specific retry paths.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen reflow fails
findings.evidence: At a 360px visual viewport the document still lays out at 1000px and overflows by 640px; the viewport meta is absent in the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore width=device-width and make all page regions reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom without two-dimensional scrolling.

findings.summary: Core content is invisible to a non-JavaScript crawler
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched status 202 with only 2,007 raw bytes and 0% rendered-word coverage; title, h1, and meta description were absent and crawler view lacked retail content.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful product/navigation HTML and metadata in the initial response, with scripts enhancing rather than creating the core experience.

findings.summary: Commercial and account entry points are not safely completable
findings.evidence: Fresh anonymous product, cart, and sign-in routes returned a challenge, generic error, and not-found page respectively, preventing verification of pricing, checkout, cancellation, or reauthentication.
findings.suggestedFix: Make these routes reliable, preserve product/cart context through authentication, and show commitments and recovery actions before confirmation.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on primary controls
findings.evidence: Explicit focus probes reported outline:none/0px on search, cart, hamburger, account, and the privacy Continue Shopping control; tiny 8x4px disclosure buttons were also found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible indicators and ensure every interactive target is at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for touch.

findings.summary: Mobile loading performance misses the LCP bar
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.54s, FCP 6.03s, Speed Index 11.04s, TTI 16.42s, and performance 54; trace LCP was 3.40s in a separate desktop-like run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reduce critical CSS/script work, and validate field Core Web Vitals by template.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a heavy, highly fragmented load
findings.evidence: HAR captured 292 requests and 5.39MB transferred, including 223 images, 22 fonts, and multiple VeryHigh parser-blocking stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical dependencies, consolidate font/style delivery, add useful lazy loading, and prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Heading and focus structure is incomplete
findings.evidence: The rendered homepage has no h1 and explicit probes show most primary controls with no visible outline, despite skip links and landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a meaningful page h1 and consistent :focus-visible treatment while preserving logical landmark and tab order.

findings.summary: Crawler/mobile signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: The homepage lacks viewport meta in the rendered state and Lighthouse found a javascript:void(0) anchor; robots.txt blocks GPTBot and several paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the viewport meta, replace pseudo-links with buttons or real hrefs, and review crawler policy by intended audience.

findings.summary: Security header and cookie posture is incomplete
findings.evidence: Direct response evidence confirms HTTPS/HSTS, but no CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy was present; cookie audit found three non-Secure cookies and auth-like cookies without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and set Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite attributes appropriate to each cookie.

findings.summary: Advertising and identity-sync footprint is excessive by default
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 26 third-party cookies and long identity-sync chains; HAR attributed 283/292 requests and 5.12MB to other origins, while the page shows only a Continue Shopping consent action.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise and defer advertising/identity sync until an explicit choice, reduce vendors, and batch essential analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication entry is unavailable and modern-auth support cannot be reached
findings.evidence: The direct /ap/signin route returned a not-found page and its DOM contained no form or passkey/WebAuthn path; no permission prompt appeared on homepage load.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore sign-in routing and expose passkey-first authentication with correct autofill and contextual permission requests.

findings.summary: Privacy choice is visually one-sided
findings.evidence: The initial notice presents a prominent yellow Continue Shopping action while preference adjustment is only an inline text link; no equally prominent reject/manage choice is shown.
findings.suggestedFix: Present accept, reject, and manage choices with equal clarity and preserve the user’s decision without nagging.

findings.summary: Image delivery is materially wasteful
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 99 used legacy formats, 86 lacked responsive sources, 85 below-fold images were not lazy, and image transfer totalled 3.36MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt AVIF/WebP via picture/srcset, right-size by rendered slot, lazy-load below-fold media, and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: The page performs disproportionate background/network work
findings.evidence: The homepage made 292 requests, including 283 cross-origin requests, and Lighthouse reported 438KiB unused JS plus 213KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally fetch below-fold and third-party features, pause background work, and remove unused bundles.

findings.summary: Third-party and font/media budgets are disproportionate
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 5.12MB cross-origin transfer, 22 font requests (739.7KB), 223 image requests, and 4 media requests for the initial homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Set template budgets, self-host/subset fonts where useful, defer nonessential media, and load advertising only after an informed choice.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains white/light grey and the computed body color-scheme is normal; no prefers-color-scheme rules were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and derive surface/text/control colours with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Interest-based ads notice interrupts the initial view
findings.evidence: The initial screenshot shows a fixed notice covering the lower page before interaction, including product cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Make privacy controls compact and non-obscuring, with clear choices and dismissal that does not block browsing.

findings.summary: Dismissible UI is implemented with custom role-based forms
findings.evidence: The notice is a form role=dialog; the probe found zero <dialog>, popover, or details elements and 27 custom role=dialog nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the native dialog/popover primitives with declarative commands, correct focus management, Escape/light dismiss, and a fallback.

findings.summary: Dense chrome crowds the shopping content
findings.evidence: Desktop evidence shows two navigation rows, a large hero, four dense merchandising cards, and a fixed notice in one viewport; mobile retains a 1000px desktop canvas.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent navigation and promotional chrome, prioritise search and the most relevant products, and progressively disclose secondary controls.

findings.summary: Script work delays interactivity
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 179.5ms TBT and 300ms max potential FID; the trace observed two long tasks up to 66.12ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, defer non-critical modules, and schedule background work at lower priority.

findings.summary: Large unused JS and CSS payloads are delivered
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 438KiB unused JavaScript and 213KiB unused CSS; HAR recorded 882.7KB script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by page capability, conditionally load dependencies, and remove duplicate/unused AUI and campaign bundles.

findings.summary: ARIA semantics are invalid on important controls
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found disallowed aria-expanded on the searchbox, aria-setsize on a list, and an accessible-name mismatch on Cart.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native semantics where possible and align roles, allowed ARIA attributes, visible labels, and accessible names.

findings.summary: Image markup and sizing are unsound
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 86/100 images without dimensions, 86 without srcset, 99 legacy-format images, 18 missing alt values, and Lighthouse found six incorrect aspect ratios.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions/aspect ratios and provide responsive modern sources while preserving appropriate alt text.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser inspector issues remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found synchronous main-thread XHR, deprecated Shared Storage usage, third-party cookie inspector issues, and a 50 best-practices score.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove synchronous XHR and deprecated Shared Storage use, resolve cookie issues, and retest BFCache and inspector warnings.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defence headers are incomplete
findings.evidence: HSTS is present, but CSP/frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy were absent in captured responses; insecure/SameSite=None cookies remain.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out CSP with frame-ancestors and Trusted Types where appropriate, nosniff, strict referrer/permissions policies, and modern cookie controls.

findings.summary: Commerce capabilities are not exposed safely to agents
findings.evidence: The homepage contained no WebMCP/agentic tool registration, the raw crawler view had 0% content coverage, and robots.txt explicitly disallows GPTBot.
findings.suggestedFix: If agentic commerce is intended, expose bounded WebMCP tools/agentic forms for search, product details, cart, and checkout with confirmation gates.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS only contains reset-to-unset view-transition declarations; search/product journeys replace the page abruptly with error or challenge screens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document transitions for carousel/menu state and cross-document View Transitions for eligible retail navigation, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Carousel/navigation interactions use legacy controls without platform gesture behaviour
findings.evidence: The homepage hero is an arrow-driven carousel; DOM/CSS inspection found no active scroll-snap or overscroll gesture rules, only reset declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement carousels with scroll snap and overscroll containment while retaining buttons and keyboard operation.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not react to scroll state
findings.evidence: The long homepage keeps a fixed two-row header and no animation-timeline or scroll-state query was found in captured CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container scroll-state queries or a declarative scroll-driven header/progress affordance where the page length warrants it.

findings.summary: Overlays are custom-positioned rather than anchored platform popovers
findings.evidence: The platform probe found 27 role=dialog elements, zero native dialogs/popovers, and no active anchor positioning declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover/dialog plus CSS anchor positioning and position fallbacks for menus, tips, and transient overlays.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a client error
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a console error warning that module @m/mash loaded late.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the late module dependency/ordering issue and keep production console error-free.

findings.summary: Homepage lacks structured entity metadata
findings.evidence: The platform probe found Open Graph metadata but zero JSON-LD blocks on a public retail/organization homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD, including SearchAction only if it matches a reliable crawlable search URL.

findings.summary: No installable app metadata is exposed
findings.evidence: A service worker controls the homepage, but the runtime probe found no web app manifest. For a repeat-use commerce service, this leaves installability and offline intent undefined.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid manifest and a lightweight offline/retry fallback for browsing state, or explicitly document why installability is out of scope.
